content:
When Apple finally responded to the sharp rise in memory and other component costs, it did so ruthlessly. Some increases exceeded fifty percent, and certain memory and storage capacity upgrades even doubled in price.

These higher prices are likely to persist for years, and may never come down…

9to5Mac readers were already skeptical about whether Apple would reduce prices once component shortages eased. Over two-thirds of respondents indicated that they expected this price hike to be permanent.

A subsequent analyst report noted that supply chain pricing would not improve before 2028, and even then the improvement would be limited. It is now quite clear that the current extremely high pricing will remain for at least several years, and is likely to never return to previous levels.

If this is indeed the case, how would you respond? Would you grit your teeth and continue purchasing Apple products at the same pace? Reduce the quantity or frequency of purchases? Or take other approaches, such as choosing lower-tier models, buying refurbished units, or waiting for price drops before making a move?
